name: Aboriginal country of the Methow, Okanagan, Colville, San Poil and neighbouring tribes, taken without a treaty
citation: No treaty; Royce schedule memorandum dated 1871
nations: Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation (Colville, Lake, Sanpoil, Nespelem, Okanogan, Methow)
promises: No treaty was made. Royce records that no treaty was ever made with these tribes to extinguish their territorial rights, and that the United States simply took possession of their country except the parts set apart for them by executive order.

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission held that the Indian title of the Colville, Lake, Sanpoil, Nespelem, Okanogan and Methow tribes to their lands outside the reservation was extinguished by the United States without payment of compensation as of July 2, 1872, when the Colville Reservation was established; it found the United States never considered their aboriginal rights to those lands.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Docket 181, Opinion and Findings of Fact (4 Ind. Cl. Comm. 151 and 187, February 29, 1956)

source.title: Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation et al. v. United States, Docket 181, Opinion of the Commission (4 Ind. Cl. Comm. 187, February 29, 1956)
source.publisher: Indian Claims Commission Decisions, Oklahoma State University Library

landTaken: Royce shows as this area (532) the former country of these tribes not within the reservations of April 9 and July 2, 1872. The Commission found the petitioner tribes' non-reservation lands taken as of July 2, 1872.
compensation: Of the Docket 181 tracts, the Sanpoil-Nespelem tract (south of the Columbia), the Okanogan tract and the Methow tract (west of the Okanogan River) lie in this area; the Colville and Lakes tracts lie east of the Columbia, inside the April 9, 1872 tract (Royce area 533). The Commission's second interlocutory order of March 5, 1959 awarded the Sanpoil-Nespelem Tribe $436,000.00, the Okanogan Tribe $237,000.00 and the Methow Tribe $152,000.00, less offsets. The final judgment of March 1, 1960 allowed $61,000.00 in offsets across all five awards (the Methow offset was $6,700.00) and states a total net recovery of $1,000,000.00.
today: The Commission's award covers the six Colville tribes only; Royce's area also names the Kootenay, Pend d'Oreille and North Spokane, whose claims were not traced here.

nationVoice.nation: Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation
nationVoice.summary: The Tribes' 2023 history for educators records that a Presidential Executive Order of April 1872 set up the Colville Reservation for the tribes and bands who were not parties to any treaty, and that an order of July 2, 1872 reduced the reservation's size.

openQuestions: The date 1871-01-01 is a placeholder: Royce's entry is an undated memorandum under 1871. The Commission dated the taking July 2, 1872, the same finding used for cession-1872-07-02-methow-okanagan.

Royce's area 532 reaches into Idaho and Montana and names the Kootenay, Pend d'Oreille and North Spokane; the Docket 181 finding covers only the six Colville tribes' lands, so it does not cover the whole polygon.
The Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation's own history of the taking was not found (noted also on the 1872-07-02 record).

Audit 2026-11-08: compensation and plain.today rewritten. The Sanpoil-Nespelem, Okanogan and Methow figures are clean in the second interlocutory order (OSU id 248); the earlier text called them unreadable and named only the Methow. Which Docket 181 tracts fall in area 532 and which in area 533 is the auditor's reading of the tract descriptions in the 1959 opinion (OSU id 191: Colville tract east of the Columbia from Kettle Falls to Hunters, Lakes tract east of the Columbia to the Canadian line, Methow and Okanogan tracts west of the Okanogan River) against Royce's boundaries, not a statement of the Commission. This record, cession-1872-04-09-methow-okanagan and cession-1872-07-02-methow-okanagan rest on the same July 2, 1872 taking; read together, this record carries the Sanpoil-Nespelem, Okanogan and Methow lands and the April 9 record the Colville and Lake lands, so they do not double-count it.

plain.promised: Nothing was promised: no treaty was ever made for the land of the Methow, Okanogan, Colville, Sanpoil, Nespelem and Lake tribes.
plain.happened: The Indian Claims Commission found in 1956 that the United States took their lands outside the Colville Reservation without paying for them, as of July 2, 1872.
plain.today: In 1959 the Commission awarded $436,000.00 for the Sanpoil-Nespelem lands, $237,000.00 for the Okanogan lands and $152,000.00 for the Methow lands in this area, less offsets. Other tribes named in this area were not traced.
